subject: VPB broker & islanded control-plane: scope, egress, and test plan

Subject: VPB broker & islanded control-plane: scope, egress, and test plan

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this. Were starting the architecture review for FinLytics' private deployment and want to validate the pattern were proposing: an "islanded" control plane (no direct internet egress) with a small broker layer that mediates control-plane commands to the data-plane clusters. Our compliance team needs clear evidence of network demarcation, egress controls, and an automated canary plan before we sign off.

High-level constraints: 
- Control plane must not initiate outbound connections to third-party endpoints; all third-party interactions must be via an approved proxy or the customer's jump host.
- Management traffic should be auditable and KMS-backed.
- Latency SLOs are strict for model rollouts (p95 < 300ms for control events).
- SOC 2 + PCI scoping: we need clear diagrams and an acceptance test plan.

I attached the initial customer YAML and a short whitepaper on our compliance asks. Can you and your infra/security team review and respond with:
1) A recommended broker model (transit gateway vs. managed proxy) and why,
2) Egress proofing approach (NAT, static egress, DPI, cert pinning),
3) A short canary test plan and evidence artifacts we should produce for SOC2 audit.

Proposed meeting: Wed 4/26 10:00 PT if that works.

Thanks,
Ian
Ian Long

Subject: Re: VPB broker & islanded control-plane: scope, egress, and test plan

Ian — appreciate the clear constraints. Quick acknowledgement and initial take below. I also attached a short proposal (vpc-broker-proposal.pdf) that outlines two candidate patterns.

High-level recommendation (summary):
- Broker pattern: lightweight managed broker sitting in the customer VPC as an appliance (containerized) that terminates mutual TLS from Redwood control-plane agents, enforces ACLs, and forwards only signed operations to the data-plane. We prefer this over a full transit GW when the customer wants tight auditability and minimal blast radius.
- Egress proofing: recommend zero-trust egress for control-plane hosts — traffic only allowed to customer-owned jump/proxy or a vetted egress endpoint (no direct 0.0.0.0/0). Use VPC route tables + security groups and an egress proxy that requires mTLS.
- KMS & secrets: integrate with customer KMS (bring-your-own-key). We will only request short-lived session tokens; key operations (signing) remain in-customer.

Open questions we need answered before finalizing:
- Can you confirm whether the customer will host a VPC-managed proxy (squid/privoxy) or expects Redwood to provide a broker appliance?
- Are there FIPS/HSM requirements, or will a cloud KMS suffice?
- What retention window for audit logs are you targeting for SOC2? 90/365 days?

Next steps:
1) Marissa will drop a diagram of the proposed islanded control-plane (attached).
2) Well put together a minimal canary plan (smoke + regression prompts) and a list of artifacts for audit.
3) Confirm Wed 4/26 10:00 PT — Ill send a calendar invite.

Quick attachment list: vpc-broker-proposal.pdf (proposal + short risk matrix).

—
Grace O'Connor

Ian / Grace — attaching an initial diagram and a few concrete guardrails. See islanded-controlplane-diagram.v1.png. Notes below: 

Design notes (concrete):
- Network layout: control-plane subnet (private, no IGW) -> broker subnet (appliance) -> data-plane subnets. Broker has two NICs: one facing control-plane (mTLS only) and one facing data-plane with strict ACL. Control-plane agents authenticate with mTLS + JWK-signed JWTs.
- Egress enforcement: route control-plane subnet to a customer-owned egress proxy. If the customer cannot host one, we propose a dedicated NAT box that only permits outbound to pre-approved artifact endpoints (hash pinning + IP allowlist).
- Observability: broker emits signed audit events to a local S3-compatible store in-customer VPC; Redwood ships aggregated index metadata (no raw logs) to our control plane only if customer explicitly enables it (opt-in).
- Certificate rotation & KMS: certificate private keys are stored in customer HSM when available; otherwise, AES-wrapped keys in customer KMS. Rotation scheduled via the broker with zero-downtime rolling updates.
- Canary approach (overview): canary flow lives entirely in-customer VPC. Steps: deploy a canary model instance -> push a controlled config change via broker -> assert metrics (latency, error rate, rollout success). Artifacts: signed runbook, raw audit logs (stored in customer S3), composite canary report (CSV/Excel).

Port/Protocol suggestions (initial):
- ControlPlane <-> Broker: TLS 443 (mTLS), port 8443 for internal agent endpoints if behind sidecar.
- Broker <-> DataPlane: TCP 50051 for control RPCs (gRPC) with mTLS.
- Metrics/telemetry push: push to a pull-only metrics collector using an internal aggregator; do not allow direct metrics egress to Redwood SaaS without opt-in.

Attachments: islanded-controlplane-diagram.v1.png (annotated), small config snippets in the proposal.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: islanded-controlplane-diagram.v1.png)
